audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys[] narrate Mel winning levels 2-5 and 'late evens out', while win[1..3] and win[5..6] on the same page say Skill/Wukong/Wukong/Wukong/Wukong. The page renders two different answers per row.
audit.why: phases[].side and win[] already agree (Mel, Skill, Wukong, Wukong, Mel, Wukong, Wukong) and that ordering matches the 57.49% win rate over 327 games. The whys are the layer that is out of step, so the whys move, not the sides.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0..6] so each one states the case for the side already recorded in win[N]; no side or rating flipped, so no atomic chart group is required.

audit.why: Spike structure is intact: Mel spikes at Solar Snare rank-ups, level 6 (Golden Eclipse 120/100/80s), and first item; Wukong spikes at levels 2-3 for the full pattern, Black Cleaver, and the two-item side-lane window. spikes[] already has four entries, so no create-only repair is needed.
audit.corrected: Left spike timings as they stand; corrected the mechanical claim inside spikes[0].text (see point 4) without moving any 'when'.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text and wants.foe[1] both claim Rebuttal (W) 'reflects your E-Q engage back at you' and 'can stun if she catches your commit'. Neither is true. Riot's text for Rebuttal: a barrier that reflects enemy PROJECTILES, prevents her taking damage, and grants movement speed. There is no stun anywhere in Mel's kit, and Wukong's Nimbus Strike and Crushing Blow are not projectiles, so they are never reflected — they simply do nothing while she is immune.
audit.why: Telling a Wukong that his engage gets thrown back at him teaches him to never engage; the truth is the opposite — his engage is safe to throw, it just needs to land after the 38s W rather than into it.
audit.corrected: Restated Rebuttal as damage immunity plus projectile reflect, gave its real cooldown (38/35/33/29/26s), and reframed the advice as baiting it with the clone. Also named Golden Eclipse rather than calling the ultimate 'Overwhelm' (Overwhelm is the passive stack that R consumes), and gave Solar Snare its real 1000 range and 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Solar Snare as matchup-defining but gives no number, and never mentions Rebuttal at all — which is by far the longest punishable cooldown in her kit.
audit.why: 38s at rank 1 is an enormous window for a melee; 'engage on her W cooldown' is the whole matchup and it was not on the page.
audit.corrected: Put both real cooldowns into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mel is referred to as 'he'/'his' in tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.trading, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d and report[3].t.
audit.why: Reads as generated filler and undermines trust in the rest of the page.

notes: Mirror note carried over: the mel-side file (audits/top/mel__wukong.json) reports all seven full.phases[].side reading 'Wukong' with 'why' text describing Mel winning. That is the mel-side file, not this one — this direction's phases[].side and win[] already agree row for row, so nothing here needs an atomic chart group. Rebuttal reflecting Wukong's E-Q and 'stunning' was a fabrication on the page and is the single most important correction in this file. Not asserted anywhere, because the kit text cannot settle it: whether Solar Snare's root is cleansable/QSS-able or reduced by tenacity, and whether Rebuttal's immunity stops Cyclone's knockup from displacing her.
